0ac72672276bc8627c2c4879a433281f3158e2be: The firm failed to clean equipment and utensils at appropriate intervals, risking alteration of drug product safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity. Specifically, non dedicated equipment used for manufacturing multiple drug products sold in the US has not been adequately cleaned since installation. On 26 Aug 2024, inspection revealed build up of white to off white powdery materials, water droplets, wet surfaces, and black to dark colored deposits indicative of bacterial, fungal, and mold growth inside Air Purification Units (APUs), on and after HEPA filters in ducts, and chambers of randomly selected modules (e.g., Module XX ID: GGP/MA/035). Swab samples collected on 27 Aug 2024 from these areas showed drug substances above acceptance limits by HPLC and UV spectroscopy, indicating cross contamination risk among products manufactured on the same equipment. Unknown chromatographic peaks with area responses exceeding known active peaks were not identified or accounted for, increasing uncertainty of contamination sources. Microbial swabs from APUs collected on 27 and 29 Aug 2024 revealed TNTC fungal, bacterial, and Total Viable Particulate Count colonies, demonstrating microbial contamination inside APUs that could be carried by high velocity air into manufacturing areas, potentially contaminating products. Despite these findings, Field Alert Reports (FARs) were issued for some but not all affected drug products, violating SOP No. GGQA067 ("Handling of Field Alert Reports"), and no risk or impact assessment was performed regarding microbial contamination of distributed batches. Additional swab sampling on 01 and 02 Sep 2024 from equipment surfaces in other modules confirmed presence of drug substances above acceptance limits and unidentified chromatographic peaks, again indicating cross contamination potential; however, no FARs were filed for these products. Preventative maintenance (PM) procedures for APUs were deficient; SOP No. GGMN212 ("PROCEDURE TO PERFORM HEPA FILTER INTEGRITY TEST AND NON VIABLE PARTICLE COUNT TEST FOR PROCESS EQUIPMENTS") lacked Quality Unit responsibilities for verifying conditions of ducts, HEPA filters, and APUs during PM. As a result, Engineering replaced HEPA filters per schedule without assessing or investigating powdery deposits or contamination risks, including compromised HEPA filter integrity observed on 26 Aug 2024. Swab results confirmed presence of active drug compounds and TNTC microbial colonies in these areas, yet no investigations or risk assessments were conducted. Cleaning of processing equipment was inadequately performed and documented. During Type B cleaning on 26 Aug 2024 prior to manufacturing XX Tablets USP XX mg, significant material remained on equipment walls despite checklist completion, posing risk of cross contamination via material dislodgement into batches. On 27 Aug 2024, Type A cleaning of compression equipment showed visible residual powder on punches and dies from prior batches. Additional undocumented cleaning was performed later the same day, representing a failure in cleaning record documentation. These deficiencies compromise cleaning effectiveness and traceability, increasing contamination risk. Overall, the firm’s failures include inadequate cleaning and maintenance of manufacturing equipment and APUs, lack of effective oversight by Quality Unit during PM, failure to identify and investigate chemical and microbial contamination, incomplete and undocumented cleaning procedures, and insufficient adherence to SOPs for field alert reporting. These deficiencies pose significant risks of cross contamination and microbial contamination, threatening drug product quality and patient safety.

4015d419414dc333481cfdf318b45c2c42152d42: The firm’s procedures to prevent microbiological contamination in sterile drug products lack adequate validation of the aseptic process, particularly regarding airflow patterns and environmental monitoring. Some airflow visualization videos (AFP21 003, 03/15/2021) documented stationary air zones within the ISO 5 area, indicating potential disruption of uni directional or downward airflow critical for contamination control. Although air velocity checks are routinely performed, these airflow pattern concerns present a significant contamination risk. Environmental monitoring (EM) sampling locations lack evaluation or rationale for their selection. The Associate Director of Microbiology confirmed no assessment has been conducted to justify EM sampling sites for viable and non viable particles in ISO 5, 6, and 7 areas. Likewise, the rationale for fungal flora sampling locations and frequency per QML 1403 (SOP 011350, effective 06/21/2021) is absent, and no additional microbiological data exists for mold presence or absence in classified or CNC areas. Moreover, mold isolate characterization is deficient; microbiologists do not perform colony morphology or other identification per QML 1020 (SOP 011281, 10/07/2019), limiting understanding of contamination sources. Non viable particle (NVP) monitoring in the aseptic ISO 5 areas is conducted only at the end of filling runs rather than during dynamic operations, contrary to environmental monitoring procedure CORP 0017 (05/18/2020). This practice precludes real time assessment of contamination risk during operations. NVP monitoring equipment is positioned above door heights and not at the working height where personnel transfer glass vials, further limiting relevance of data collected. The firm’s SOP QML 1105 (SOP 01130, v17.0, 06/21/2021) requires end of run sampling, yet this conflicts with CORP 0017’s guidance that dynamic sampling better represents contamination risk, creating procedural inconsistency. Disinfectant efficacy studies on materials of construction for glass vial handling and filling equipment are absent. The Sanitization Program SOP 010031 (v27.0) mandates cleaning to control particles and microorganisms in ISO Class 5 and 6 areas, but without disinfectant efficacy data on critical surfaces, assurance of microbial control is lacking. Personnel monitoring practices were reduced without risk assessment. Since June 2020, personnel monitoring was discontinued during non production times in ISO 5/6 areas, despite historical data showing multiple microbial excursion events linked to non production personnel activities (six excursions for an environmental monitoring tech, five for a QC chemist since 2017). Additionally, glove palm sampling was removed from monitoring in 2020 despite 23 excursions detected between 2017 and 2020 involving fungal and bacterial recovery, some prompting product recalls. Gowning practices do not adequately control particulate and bacterial transfer. Scrubs of different colors for classified and non classified areas are stored together; changing rooms combine lockers, restrooms, and visibly dirty wooden benches with unaddressed cleaning procedures. Personnel wearing factory green scrubs can access multiple facility areas, including offices and restrooms, without changing gowns, and one observed street jacket over scrubs had pants touching the parking lot ground, risking contamination. Both green and blue scrubs share entry points between classified and non classified production corridors, with no personnel or environmental monitoring performed at these critical transition points. The number of allowable scrub washes and reuse is unspecified, and laundry inspection records are lacking. These deficiencies collectively indicate inadequate validation and control of aseptic processing conditions, environmental monitoring, personnel gowning, and monitoring practices, placing sterile drug product integrity at risk. This observation was repeated from the prior inspection ending 08/30/2019.

8b33b3f1c5b7028caf5208b2bd21d4e5dcff0cd6: The firm’s Quality Assurance and Quality Control units failed to ensure appropriate laboratory determination of finished drug product conformity to final specifications, compromising accuracy and reliability of analytical testing methods.
